codebase_map.architecture_summary: Python FastAPI monolith with 7 modules. The API layer exposes REST and SSE endpoints protected by JWT middleware. Business logic lives in tier1 (orchestrator, indexer, scanner, reporter). External integrations (GitHub, OpenRouter/LLM, Supabase) are in services. Sandbox execution isolates repository analysis. Global in-memory state is used for SSE event buses and webhook replay detection, creating scalability and reliability risks. The architecture lacks a clean service abstraction layer — routes directly import database clients and domain objects from tier1.
key_patterns: FastAPI dependency injection for request handling
Pydantic v2 models for request/response validation
SSE (Server-Sent Events) for real-time scan progress
Background tasks for async scan execution
Global in-memory dictionaries for shared state (anti-pattern)
Direct database access in route handlers (no repository pattern)
Tier1 business logic imported directly into route handlers

findings.title: Unbounded In-Memory SSE Event Bus Causes Memory Leak and Horizontal Scaling Failure
findings.description: The global `event_buses` dictionary in api/routes/_sse.py stores scan events indefinitely. Entries are added when a scan starts (audit.py) but never removed after the SSE stream completes or the scan finishes. This causes unbounded memory growth under sustained load. Additionally, in horizontally scaled deployments, clients connected to different instances will miss events since each instance maintains its own in-memory store. Multiple workers (security, quality, architecture across both waves) independently flagged this as critical/high severity with high confidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace in-memory event_buses with a Redis pub/sub or Redis list with TTL expiration. For single-instance deployments as an interim fix, add cleanup in the _event_generator finally block (del event_buses[scan_id]) and implement a periodic background task that removes entries older than 1 hour. Ensure cleanup happens on scan_complete and scan_error events.

findings.title: Missing Authorization Check on SSE Status Endpoint — Any User Can Monitor Any Scan
findings.description: The GET /status/{scan_id} SSE endpoint in api/routes/status.py only checks if the scan_id exists in event_buses but does not verify that the requesting user owns or has access to that scan. Any authenticated user can monitor real-time progress, findings, and agent logs of any other user's scan by guessing or obtaining a UUID. The request.state.user_id is available from middleware but unused for authorization. Flagged by two independent security workers with high confidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Before streaming, query the database to verify that the scan_id belongs to a project owned by request.state.user_id. Raise HTTP 403 if ownership check fails. Example: scan = await db.get_scan_report(scan_id, user_id); if not scan: raise HTTPException(403).

findings.title: OAuth State Secret Falls Back to JWT Secret — Cryptographic Key Confusion
findings.description: In api/routes/github_oauth.py, the _state_secret() function returns settings.supabase_jwt_secret as a fallback when github_oauth_state_secret is not set. Reusing the JWT secret for OAuth state HMAC means: (1) compromising the JWT secret also compromises OAuth flows, (2) the secrets may have different rotation schedules, and (3) if neither is configured, the system may fail unsafely. Flagged by two independent security workers.

locations.snippet:
def _state_secret() -> str:
    return settings.github_oauth_state_secret or settings.supabase_jwt_secret

findings.suggested_fix: Require github_oauth_state_secret to be explicitly configured. Remove the fallback to supabase_jwt_secret. Add a startup validation check that raises an error if OAuth is enabled but the state secret is not set. Document the required environment variable.

findings.title: Broken Access Control — IDOR on Fix Endpoint Allows Cross-User Remediation Trigger
findings.description: The POST /api/fix endpoint in api/routes/fix.py fetches an action_item using user_id for ownership, but then fetches the associated project and scan_report without verifying they belong to the same user. An attacker could potentially trigger FORGE remediation on resources belonging to other users by manipulating action_item_id relationships. The scan_report is fetched with user_id but project is fetched without ownership verification. Two workers flagged this independently.

locations.snippet:
action_item = await db.get_action_item(request_body.action_item_id, user_id)
...
project = await db.get_project(project_id)
...
scan_report = await db.get_scan_report(scan_report_id, user_id)

findings.suggested_fix: After fetching project, explicitly verify project['user_id'] == user_id or that the project is linked to the user. After fetching scan_report, verify scan_report['user_id'] == user_id before proceeding. Raise HTTP 403 on any ownership mismatch.

findings.title: Rate Limiting Bypass via IP Spoofing
findings.description: The rate limiter in api/middleware/rate_limit.py uses slowapi's get_remote_address which extracts the client IP from request.client.host. When deployed behind a reverse proxy, attackers can spoof X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP headers to bypass per-IP rate limits. This affects all rate-limited endpoints. Flagged by two independent security workers.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement a custom key_func that uses authenticated user_id for rate limiting on authenticated endpoints. For a proxy-aware IP approach, configure trusted proxy IPs and use the last untrusted IP in X-Forwarded-For. Example: def user_id_key(request): return request.state.user_id.

findings.title: Non-Atomic Quota Check Creates Race Condition — Users Can Exceed Monthly Report Cap
findings.description: In api/routes/audit.py, the quota check (reports_generated >= tier1_monthly_report_cap) and the increment (db.increment_free_reports_generated) are non-atomic. Under concurrent requests, multiple users could pass the check simultaneously and all increment past the cap. This allows users to exceed their monthly report quota. Combined with the thread-unsafe global _scan_start_counter, concurrent behavior is unpredictable.

locations.snippet:
reports_generated = int(usage_row.get("reports_generated") or 0)
if reports_generated >= settings.tier1_monthly_report_cap:

findings.suggested_fix: Use a database-level atomic increment with conditional check (e.g., Supabase RPC with SELECT FOR UPDATE, or PostgreSQL atomic increment with RETURNING + check). The increment should only succeed if the current count is below the cap.

findings.title: Webhook Replay Detection Uses In-Memory Storage — Ineffective in Multi-Instance Deployments
findings.description: The _seen_deliveries dictionary in api/routes/webhook.py stores delivery IDs in process memory. In multi-instance deployments, each instance tracks deliveries independently, so replay attacks succeed against any instance that hasn't seen the delivery. The dictionary also grows unbounded during the replay window. Flagged by architecture and security workers across both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace in-memory _seen_deliveries with Redis SET with TTL (set NX with expiry equal to replay window). This provides atomic check-and-set, distributed state, and automatic expiration. For single-instance deployments, add a maximum size cap with LRU eviction.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on Onboarding and SSE Status Endpoints
findings.description: The POST /api/onboarding/org endpoint has no @limiter.limit decorator unlike other sensitive endpoints. The GET /api/status/{scan_id} SSE endpoint also lacks rate limiting, allowing unlimited concurrent SSE connections which could exhaust server file descriptors and memory. Both gaps were identified by security workers.

locations.snippet:
@router.get("/status/{scan_id}")
async def stream_status(scan_id: UUID, request: Request):

findings.suggested_fix: Add @limiter.limit(rate_limit_string()) decorator to both save_org_onboarding and stream_status endpoints. For SSE, additionally consider per-user concurrent connection tracking to prevent connection flooding.

findings.title: DRY Violation — utc_now() Duplicated Across Three Model Files
findings.description: The utc_now() function is defined identically in models/builds.py, models/program.py, and models/runtime.py. models/agent_log.py uses an inline lambda for the same logic. Any change to timestamp handling requires updating 3-4 locations. This was independently flagged by architecture and quality workers across both waves with very high confidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Create models/_utils.py with a single utc_now() implementation. Update all four files to import from it. Replace the lambda in agent_log.py with Field(default_factory=utc_now).

findings.title: Missing Input Length Constraints on Critical Model Fields — DoS and Data Integrity Risk
findings.description: Multiple Pydantic models accept unbounded string fields: AgentLogEntry.message, Finding.description/code_snippet, ActionItem.fix_steps, ProbeResult.stdout/stderr, SecretCreateRequest.value. Without length constraints, malicious clients can send arbitrarily large payloads causing memory exhaustion, storage bloat, or downstream processing failures. Multiple workers flagged this across models and API segments.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Field constraints: message=Field(max_length=10000), code_snippet=Field(default=None, max_length=5000), fix_steps list items max_length=500 with max 50 items, SecretCreateRequest.value=Field(min_length=1, max_length=65536), stdout/stderr=Field(max_length=100000). Add max_length to title/description fields as well.

findings.title: Inconsistent Status Representation — String Literals vs Enums in Models
findings.description: RuntimeSession uses Literal string types for status ('bootstrapped', 'running', 'completed', 'errored') while similar models like BuildStatus use Enum. ActionItem.effort is a plain string with comment '# quick | moderate | significant' but no enforcement. DebtItem.severity is a plain string defaulting to 'medium' while Finding.severity uses the Severity enum. This inconsistency increases risk of invalid data and typos.
findings.suggested_fix: Create an EffortLevel enum (quick/moderate/significant) and RuntimeStatus enum. Use Severity enum from findings.py for DebtItem.severity. Apply these consistently across all models that use these concepts.

findings.title: Direct Database Access in Route Handlers — No Repository Abstraction
findings.description: All route handlers (audit.py, fix.py, onboarding.py, primer.py, github_oauth.py) directly import services.supabase_client as db and call methods on it. This creates tight coupling between the presentation layer and persistence layer. Routes cannot be tested without a Supabase connection, and switching database implementations requires modifying all route files. Flagged by multiple architecture workers across both waves.

locations.snippet: from services import supabase_client as db
from services import supabase_client as db
from services import supabase_client as db
from services import supabase_client as db
from services import supabase_client as db

findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a service/repository abstraction layer. Create FastAPI dependency functions (using Depends()) that provide a database interface. This enables dependency injection for testing and hides the Supabase implementation detail behind a stable interface.

findings.title: Route Handlers Directly Instantiate Tier1 Domain Objects — Layering Violation
findings.description: api/routes/audit.py directly imports and instantiates DeterministicIndexer, Tier1Orchestrator, and quota functions from the tier1 module. This violates clean architecture: the API presentation layer should not contain or know about internal business logic implementation details. It makes routes untestable in isolation and creates tight coupling. Flagged by two architecture workers across both waves.

locations.snippet:
from tier1.indexer import DeterministicIndexer
from tier1.orchestrator import Tier1Orchestrator
from tier1.quota import get_quota_status, utc_month_key

findings.suggested_fix: Create an AuditService class that encapsulates tier1 orchestration. The route handler should call audit_service.start_scan(...) rather than directly instantiating Tier1Orchestrator. This service can be injected via FastAPI's Depends() for testability.

findings.title: Thread-Unsafe Global Counter for Cleanup Scheduling
findings.description: _scan_start_counter in api/routes/audit.py is a global mutable variable incremented without locks in an async context. Under concurrent requests this can cause race conditions, missed cleanups, and non-deterministic behavior. The counter also doesn't survive process restarts and doesn't work in multi-process deployments. Flagged by architecture and quality workers across both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace counter-based cleanup with time-based scheduling: store last_cleanup_at timestamp and trigger cleanup if more than N minutes have elapsed. Alternatively, use APScheduler or FastAPI lifespan events to schedule periodic cleanup as a background task independent of request handling.

findings.title: Dynamic Import Inside Background Task Function
findings.description: In api/routes/fix.py, trigger_forge_remediate is imported inside the _run_forge_fix function rather than at module level. This delays import errors until runtime execution, adds overhead on every invocation, and hides the dependency from static analysis tools. Flagged by architecture and quality workers.

locations.snippet:
async def _run_forge_fix(...):
    from services.forge_bridge import trigger_forge_remediate

findings.suggested_fix: Move the import to the top of the module. If the import is optional (FORGE feature flag), handle ImportError at module level with a clear warning and set the function reference to None, checking it before use.

findings.title: Missing URL Validation on BuildRun.repo_url in Models
findings.description: BuildRun.repo_url in models/builds.py is a plain str with no URL format validation, inconsistent with AuditRequest.repo_url which uses Pydantic's HttpUrl. This inconsistency allows malformed URLs to be stored in build records and passed to downstream services. Multiple workers flagged this across both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Change BuildRun.repo_url to use Pydantic's HttpUrl type: from pydantic import HttpUrl. Apply consistently across all models that accept repository URLs.

findings.title: Prompt Injection Risk — Repository Data Interpolated Directly into LLM Prompt
findings.description: In api/routes/primer.py, repository data (file_tree_sample, dependency_sample, npm_scripts) from user-controlled repositories is interpolated directly into the LLM prompt string. A malicious repository could contain content designed to override the system prompt instructions (prompt injection), potentially causing the LLM to return harmful or misleading analysis. The 15000-character truncation does not prevent injection.

locations.snippet:
prompt = (
    "You are Agent_Primer. Summarize this repository context in 4 short bullets:\n"
    ...
    f"{json.dumps(primer_json)[:15000]}"
)

findings.suggested_fix: Use a structured JSON format to clearly separate system instructions from repository data (already partially done with json.dumps). Consider adding a prompt prefix/suffix that instructs the model to treat the JSON as data-only. Validate and sanitize repository-sourced strings to remove content that looks like system instructions.

findings.title: High Cyclomatic Complexity in _tier1_preflight Function
findings.description: The _tier1_preflight function in api/routes/audit.py contains excessive nested branching with multiple conditions for onboarding, project count, report quota, and LOC cap validation. This makes the function difficult to test comprehensively and maintain. A single function handles too many distinct validation concerns.
findings.suggested_fix: Refactor into focused validation functions: _validate_onboarding(), _validate_project_limit(), _validate_report_quota(), _validate_loc_cap(). Each raises a specific HTTPException variant. _tier1_preflight becomes a coordinator calling these in sequence.

findings.title: Missing Onboarding Check in Primer Endpoint
findings.description: The POST /api/primer endpoint does not verify that the user has completed onboarding before proceeding, unlike the audit endpoint which enforces this in _tier1_preflight. This allows users to access primer functionality without completing required setup steps, bypassing a business rule that should be consistently enforced.
findings.suggested_fix: Add at the beginning of run_primer: if not await db.is_onboarding_complete(user_id): raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail={'code': 'onboarding_required', 'message': 'Please complete onboarding first.'}).

findings.title: Hardcoded Magic Numbers Scattered Across Multiple Files
findings.description: Multiple hardcoded numeric values throughout the codebase lack documentation or configuration: max_idle=600 in status.py, _CLEANUP_EVERY_N_SCANS=5 in audit.py, file tree limits (350, 200, 40), timeout values (30, 15), prompt character limit (15000), and LLM max_tokens (280) in primer.py. These reduce configurability and maintainability.
findings.suggested_fix: Move magic numbers to config.py/Settings class with descriptive names and default values: SSE_MAX_IDLE_SECONDS=600, CLEANUP_SCAN_INTERVAL=5, PRIMER_MAX_FILE_TREE=350, etc. Document the rationale for each value.

findings.title: Broad Exception Handling Masks Error Details
findings.description: Multiple routes use broad `except Exception:` clauses that log the error but provide generic responses to callers. This prevents differentiated error handling and makes debugging harder. In audit.py, the background task catch-all converts all errors to the same 'scan failed' message. Inconsistent patterns also exist: some routes re-raise HTTPException explicitly (redundant), while others catch all exceptions including HTTPException.

locations.snippet:
except Exception:
    logger.exception("Tier1 audit background task failed for scan %s", scan_id)

except Exception as exc:
    logger.exception("Failed to resolve repo info for primer")

findings.suggested_fix: Catch specific exception types (httpx.HTTPStatusError, ValueError, asyncio.TimeoutError) and handle each appropriately. Remove redundant HTTPException re-raise patterns — let them propagate naturally. Add a global exception handler in main.py for unhandled exceptions with consistent error response format.

findings.title: Sandbox Command Execution Without Repo URL Allowlist Validation
findings.description: The primer endpoint passes user-supplied repo_url directly to SandboxManager.provision() and executes shell commands (find, ls, git) on the cloned repository. There is no validation that the URL is from an allowed domain (e.g., github.com). A malicious actor could supply URLs pointing to attacker-controlled repositories containing scripts or symlinks designed to exploit the sandbox environment.

locations.snippet:
await sandbox_mgr.provision(scan_id, repo_info.clone_url)
tree = await sandbox_mgr.exec(scan_id, "find . -type f ...")

findings.suggested_fix: Add domain allowlist validation before provisioning: ensure repo_url hostname is in an allowed set (e.g., ['github.com', 'gitlab.com']). Validate that the URL scheme is https. Consider adding repository ownership verification via the GitHub API before cloning.

findings.title: Inconsistent Enum Naming Conventions Across Models
findings.description: Enum value naming is inconsistent: BuildStatus uses lowercase ('pending', 'completed'), GateType uses SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE ('MERGE_GATE', 'TEST_GATE'), LogLevel includes 'success' (not a standard log level). This makes the API contract unpredictable for consumers and increases the risk of incorrect comparisons.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize all Enum values to lowercase. Remove 'success' from LogLevel or rename to a custom 'AppLogLevel' to clarify it's application-specific. Document enum conventions in a CONTRIBUTING guide.

findings.title: Models Lack Clear __init__.py Public API Surface
findings.description: The models directory either lacks or has a minimal __init__.py that does not declare __all__. External code must know internal file structure to import models (e.g., from models.builds import BuildRun). This exposes internal organization and makes refactoring — such as moving models between files — a breaking change for all importers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit __all__ to models/__init__.py exporting all public model classes. Update importers to use package-level imports (from models import BuildRun) to decouple from internal file organization.

findings.title: LLM Prompt Character Truncation May Cause Silent Context Loss
findings.description: In api/routes/primer.py, primer_json is truncated to 15000 characters before being sent to the LLM. This character-based truncation can cut in the middle of JSON structures, causing malformed context. Many LLM APIs count tokens (not characters), and 15000 characters may exceed token limits for some models while being over-conservative for others.
findings.suggested_fix: Instead of truncating the raw JSON string, selectively include the most important fields and truncate individual list fields (file_tree, dependencies) to conservative sizes. Consider using a token counter library if available. Validate that the resulting prompt is valid JSON if the LLM expects structured input.

decisions.rationale: Critical memory leak and scaling issue. Requires changes to _sse.py, audit.py, and status.py. Well-understood fix (cleanup on stream end + TTL). 2-3 files.
High severity auth bypass. Single file change (status.py) requiring a DB query for ownership check. Scoped fix.
Deterministic fix: remove fallback in _state_secret() and add startup validation. Single file, single function change.
Auth/IDOR issue. Requires understanding the DB schema and adding ownership checks in fix.py. Scoped to 1 file but needs careful implementation.
Rate limiting bypass. Requires custom key_func implementation in rate_limit.py, touching middleware that affects all routes.
Race condition requiring atomic DB operation. Affects audit.py and potentially supabase_client.py. Needs DB-level coordination.
Webhook replay detection needs Redis or bounded cache. Single file webhook.py but architectural change to use external store.
Simple decorator addition on two endpoints. Deterministic, low-risk change.
Purely mechanical DRY fix: create models/_utils.py, update 4 import sites. No logic changes.
Adding Field constraints across multiple model files (5-7 files). Requires judgment on appropriate limits but each change is localized.
Creating new Enum types and updating existing models. Affects models/findings.py, builds.py, runtime.py. 3 files.
Architectural refactor requiring repository abstraction layer. Affects 5+ route files and would introduce new service/repository modules.
Architectural refactor requiring AuditService extraction. Touches audit.py and tier1 modules. 5-10 files.
Replace global counter with time-based approach. Primarily audit.py, possibly adding APScheduler config.
Mechanical fix: move import to module level in fix.py. Single line change.
Type change from str to HttpUrl in models/builds.py. Single field change.
Prompt injection mitigation in primer.py. Requires careful handling to not break LLM functionality.
Refactoring _tier1_preflight in audit.py into smaller functions. Scoped to 1-2 files.
Simple guard clause addition in primer.py. Single function, 3 lines.
Move constants to config.py Settings class. Mechanical change across ~3 files.
Exception handling standardization across multiple route files. Requires judgment on appropriate exception types.
URL allowlist validation in primer.py. Scoped fix but requires security-aware implementation.
Enum value standardization in model files. Mechanical rename with migration path for existing data.
Add __all__ to models/__init__.py. Single file, mechanical change.
Prompt construction refactor in primer.py. Requires understanding of LLM token limits and desired context selection.

items.title: Create shared utc_now utility and eliminate duplication
acceptance_criteria: models/_utils.py exists with single utc_now() function
All three model files import utc_now from models._utils
agent_log.py uses Field(default_factory=utc_now) instead of lambda
No duplicate utc_now definitions remain
All existing tests pass
items.approach: Create models/_utils.py with utc_now function. Update imports in builds.py, program.py, runtime.py. Replace lambda in agent_log.py with utc_now reference.

items.title: Require explicit OAuth state secret — remove JWT secret fallback
acceptance_criteria: _state_secret() raises configuration error if github_oauth_state_secret is not set
No fallback to supabase_jwt_secret
Startup validation in config.py checks for required OAuth secret when OAuth is enabled
Clear error message guides operators to set the required env var
items.approach: Modify _state_secret() to raise HTTPException or startup error if github_oauth_state_secret is empty. Add validator to Settings class in config.py.

items.title: Add rate limiting to onboarding and SSE status endpoints
acceptance_criteria: @limiter.limit(rate_limit_string()) applied to save_org_onboarding
@limiter.limit(rate_limit_string()) applied to stream_status
Rate limiting tests pass for both endpoints
items.approach: Add @limiter.limit(rate_limit_string()) decorator to both endpoints following the same pattern as other rate-limited routes.

items.title: Move forge_bridge import to module level in fix.py
acceptance_criteria: trigger_forge_remediate imported at module top level
ImportError handled gracefully at module load if FORGE is not available
No dynamic imports inside function bodies
items.approach: Move import statement to top of fix.py. Wrap in try/except ImportError if FORGE is optional, setting function reference to None and checking before use.

items.title: Use HttpUrl type for BuildRun.repo_url
acceptance_criteria: BuildRun.repo_url uses pydantic HttpUrl type
Existing model tests pass with URL validation
Invalid URL strings rejected with validation error
items.approach: Add from pydantic import HttpUrl import. Change repo_url: str to repo_url: HttpUrl in BuildRun model.

items.title: Add onboarding check to primer endpoint
acceptance_criteria: run_primer checks is_onboarding_complete before proceeding
Returns HTTP 403 with code 'onboarding_required' if not complete
Test coverage for both onboarded and non-onboarded users
items.approach: Add guard clause at start of run_primer: check db.is_onboarding_complete(user_id) and raise HTTPException(403) if False.

items.title: Move magic numbers to configuration
acceptance_criteria: SSE_MAX_IDLE_SECONDS, CLEANUP_SCAN_INTERVAL, PRIMER_MAX_FILE_TREE etc. defined in Settings
All referenced files use settings.* instead of hardcoded numbers
Documented default values with rationale in config.py
items.approach: Add named settings fields with defaults to config.py Settings class. Replace inline literals in route files with settings.* references.

items.title: Standardize enum naming conventions
acceptance_criteria: All enum values use consistent lowercase or snake_case naming
LogLevel 'success' value documented or renamed to clarify purpose
GateType values normalized to lowercase
No breaking changes to existing consumers without migration path
items.approach: Audit all enum classes. Standardize values to lowercase. Add deprecation aliases where enum values are used externally. Update tests.

items.title: Add models/__init__.py with explicit public API exports
acceptance_criteria: models/__init__.py declares __all__ with all public model classes
Package-level imports work (from models import BuildRun)
No breaking changes to existing import sites
items.approach: Enumerate all public classes across model files. Add __all__ list and re-export statements to models/__init__.py.

items.title: Fix SSE event bus memory leak with cleanup mechanism
acceptance_criteria: event_buses entries are removed when SSE stream terminates (finally block in _event_generator)
Periodic background task cleans entries older than configurable TTL (default 1 hour)
Memory usage is bounded under sustained load
scan_complete and scan_error events trigger cleanup
items.approach: Add try/finally to _event_generator to delete the scan_id key on stream termination. Add a background cleanup task in main.py lifespan that periodically sweeps stale entries. Consider adding entry timestamp to event_buses to support TTL eviction.

items.title: Add ownership authorization check to SSE status endpoint
acceptance_criteria: stream_status queries DB to verify scan_id belongs to request.state.user_id
Returns HTTP 403 if user does not own the scan
Returns HTTP 404 if scan_id not found (existing behavior preserved)
Authorization check logged for audit purposes
items.approach: After checking event_buses, query db.get_scan_report(scan_id, user_id). If None returned, raise HTTPException(403) to avoid information disclosure about other users' scans.

items.title: Fix IDOR in fix endpoint — verify project and scan ownership
acceptance_criteria: After fetching project, verify project['user_id'] == user_id
After fetching scan_report, verify scan_report['user_id'] == user_id
HTTP 403 raised on any ownership mismatch
Test cases cover cross-user access attempts
items.approach: Add explicit ownership checks after each db.get_project() and db.get_scan_report() call. Raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail={'code': 'forbidden'}) on mismatch.

items.title: Replace IP-based rate limiting with user-ID-based limiting
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated endpoints use user_id as rate limit key
Unauthenticated endpoints (webhook) use IP with trusted proxy handling
Rate limiting cannot be bypassed by IP spoofing on authenticated endpoints
Existing rate limit tests updated
items.approach: Implement custom key_func that returns request.state.user_id for authenticated requests. Create a separate key function for the webhook endpoint using verified IP. Configure Limiter with the new key_func.

items.title: Make quota check atomic using database-level operations
acceptance_criteria: Quota check and increment are a single atomic DB operation
Concurrent requests cannot both pass the quota gate when only 1 slot remains
Returns clear error when quota is exceeded
Database function or RPC implements check-and-increment pattern
items.approach: Create a Supabase RPC function (increment_if_under_cap) that atomically checks and increments the counter. Replace the read-then-write pattern in audit.py with a single call to this function.

items.title: Make webhook replay detection distributed-safe
acceptance_criteria: Delivery ID registration uses Redis SET NX with TTL or equivalent
Works correctly in multi-instance deployments
In-memory dict _seen_deliveries removed or bounded
No memory growth from webhook replay tracking
items.approach: If Redis is available, use redis.set(delivery_id, 1, nx=True, ex=replay_window_seconds) for atomic check-and-set. As fallback for single-instance, add max-size eviction (e.g., cap at 10000 entries with oldest-first eviction).

items.title: Add input length constraints to critical model fields
acceptance_criteria: AgentLogEntry.message has max_length=10000
Finding.code_snippet has max_length=5000
Finding.description has max_length=10000
SecretCreateRequest.value has min_length=1, max_length=65536
ProbeResult.stdout/stderr have max_length=100000
ActionItem.fix_steps list items bounded
Validation tests confirm oversized inputs are rejected
items.approach: Add Field constraints to each affected field. Choose limits based on realistic maximum values. Add corresponding test cases for boundary conditions.

items.title: Standardize status and enum fields using proper Enum types
acceptance_criteria: EffortLevel enum created with quick/moderate/significant values
ActionItem.effort uses EffortLevel enum
DebtItem.severity uses Severity enum from findings.py
RuntimeSession status uses RuntimeStatus enum or Literal with documented values

remediation_plan.summary: 25 findings across 4 severity levels. Execution is organized in 6 levels. Level 1 addresses quick deterministic fixes (DRY violation, missing rate limits, OAuth secret, module-level imports, onboarding guard). Level 2 addresses model-layer improvements (URL validation, magic numbers, enum naming, access control fixes, rate limiting bypass, atomic quota, webhook replay). Level 3 addresses the critical memory leak, global state, input validation constraints, and exception handling. Level 4 handles dependent improvements (SSE auth check, prompt injection, LLM truncation, enum enforcement). Levels 5-6 are architectural refactors (repository abstraction, service layer) that significantly improve testability but are lower immediate risk. The three highest-severity security issues (F-001 memory leak, F-002 SSE auth bypass, F-004 IDOR in fix endpoint) are prioritized and unblocked. The architectural refactors (F-012, F-013) are significant efforts best scheduled after the security and quality fixes stabilize the codebase.
